i) Using Taylor series, prove the following when $x$ is a small number. Assume $f(x)$ is infinitely differentiable (everywhere): $\left|\int_0^x f(x)\,dx - x f(0)\right| \leq \frac{1}{2} C x^2$, where $|f'(x)| \leq C$. ii) Approximate the following when $x$ is a small number: $\int_0^{1/n} (n - n x^2) f(x)\,dx$. iii) You are given $g_n(x)$ which satisfies: $g_n(x) = -n^2(|x| - \frac{1}{n})$ if $|x| < \frac{1}{n}$, and $0$ otherwise (the source notes $g_n(x) = \delta(x)$, the Dirac delta function). What is $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} g_n(x) f(x)\,dx$ when $n \to 0$?

i) You are given 4 cards, with the front saying 1 or 2 and the back saying A or B. These happen independently and have an equal chance of occurring. What is the probability that if a card says 1 it also says A? Hence, generalize this for any $n$ cards $\in \mathbb{Z}^+$.
